title: Which? Gender and Case Agreement
lede: Ask a precise “which?” question by matching the noun’s gender, building the construct phrase and choosing the case required by the whole sentence.
nav: Yes/No Questions with هَلْ and أَ

items.feedback: يَوْمٌ is masculine, so use أَيّ.
سَيَّارَةٌ is feminine, so use أَيَّة.

items.prompt: What case is the noun after basic أَيّ / أَيَّة?
options: Genitive as the second term of an iḍāfa
items.feedback: أَيّ / أَيَّة is the first term of a construct phrase; the following noun is genitive.
The phrase is the direct object, so أَيَّ is accusative; كِتَابٍ remains genitive in the construct.
فِي makes أَيِّ genitive; فَصْلٍ completes the construct.

items.prompt: Which word asks for a selection from known options?
items.feedback: أَيّ / أَيَّة narrows the question to a choice.
لُغَةٌ is feminine; the nominative model is أَيَّةُ لُغَةٍ.
طَرِيقٌ is masculine.

items.prompt: Choose “which sport” as the direct object.
items.feedback: رِيَاضَةٌ is feminine, and the phrase is accusative as the direct object.
لَوْنٌ is masculine and the phrase is the nominative subject of يُنَاسِبُ.
The “which teacher” phrase is the subject, so أَيُّ is nominative.
The film is the direct object, so أَيَّ is accusative.
مِنْ requires the genitive: أَيَّةِ مَدِينَةٍ.

items.prompt: Which part stays genitive in all three basic models?
items.feedback: The following noun is the second term of the iḍāfa.
يَوْمٌ is masculine and the phrase is the subject.
Use feminine أَيَّةَ; the whole phrase is accusative while حَقِيبَةٍ is genitive.
مِنْ governs the genitive and دَوْلَةٌ is feminine.

items.prompt: Choose the best question for a known list of subjects.
items.feedback: أَيَّةَ asks for one chosen subject and matches the feminine noun.
يَوْمٌ is masculine; the basic isolated model is nominative.
سَاعَةٌ is feminine.

items.prompt: Why is the noun after أَيّ genitive?
options: It is always a direct object.
Question words force every noun accusative.
items.feedback: أَيّ / أَيَّة is the first term of the construct.
The choice phrase is the nominative subject.
Feminine and accusative as the direct object.
Feminine and genitive after فِي.

items.prompt: Which question asks for a known selection?
items.feedback: أَيّ narrows the question to one option.
أَيُّ is the first term; لَوْنٍ is genitive.
إِلَى governs the entire choice phrase.

options: Gender → sentence role/case → genitive following noun.
Translate into English first and ignore case.
items.feedback: The three-step sequence protects all required agreements.

games.e: Masculine and nominative subject; noun genitive.
Feminine and nominative subject; noun genitive.
The phrase is the accusative object.

blocks: ## “Which?” asks for a choice from a known set
Unlike a broad “what?”, أَيّ / أَيَّة points to one item, person, time or option among possibilities.
[callout] Cambridge relevance: precise choice questions occur naturally in timetables, travel, shopping, preferences and role-play follow-ups.
Secure gender agreement first, then add construct and case control.
- Keep the following noun singular and genitive in the basic model.
- Use أَيُّ / أَيَّ / أَيِّ according to sentence role.
- Distinguish “which?” from broader مَا / مَاذَا questions.
- Use known plural/dual sets and forms such as أَيُّهُمَا.
- Edit complex questions for gender, case and prepositions.
Choose the form that matches the noun before analysing case.
Choose أَيّ when the listener can select or identify one option from a set.

TABLE: Question type | Arabic model | Expected answer // Open identity: What is this? | مَا هَذَا؟ | هَذَا جِهَازٌ. // Known choice: Which device? | أَيُّ جِهَازٍ تُرِيدُ؟ | أُرِيدُ الْحَاسُوبَ. // Open action: What are you reading? | مَاذَا تَقْرَأُ؟ | أَقْرَأُ قِصَّةً. // Known choice: Which story? | أَيَّةَ قِصَّةٍ تَقْرَأُ؟ | أَقْرَأُ الْقِصَّةَ الْأُولَى.
[callout] Meaning test: can the listener reasonably point to one option, day, route, subject or item? If yes, “which?” is likely appropriate.
The interrogative form follows the grammatical gender of the noun—not the gender of the person speaking.
[callout/warning] Do not guess from meaning alone. Learn the grammatical gender with the noun. For example, طَرِيقٌ is masculine; سَاعَةٌ is feminine.
أَيّ / أَيَّة is the first term of an iḍāfa; the following noun completes its meaning and is genitive.

TABLE: First term | Second term | Whole meaning // أَيُّ | يَوْمٍ | which day // أَيَّةُ | سَاعَةٍ | which hour/time // أَيَّ | كِتَابٍ | which book // أَيَّةِ | مَدْرَسَةٍ | which school (after a preposition)
[callout] Two endings, two jobs: the ending on أَيّ / أَيَّة follows the phrase’s role in the sentence. The following noun is genitive because it is the second term of the construct.
Ask what role the whole “which + noun” phrase performs.

TABLE: Role | Masculine | Feminine | Why? // Nominative subject | أَيُّ يَوْمٍ يُنَاسِبُكَ؟ | أَيَّةُ سَاعَةٍ تُنَاسِبُكِ؟ | The choice itself performs/supplies the subject role. // Accusative object | أَيَّ كِتَابٍ قَرَأْتَ؟ | أَيَّةَ رِيَاضَةٍ تُفَضِّلِينَ؟ | The choice receives the action. // After a preposition | فِي أَيِّ فَصْلٍ تَدْرُسُ؟ | فِي أَيَّةِ مَدْرَسَةٍ تَدْرُسِينَ؟ | فِي requires the genitive.
[callout] Three-step decision: identify gender → identify the whole phrase’s role → keep the following noun genitive.
A strong question identifies the category; a strong answer identifies the selected item and explains why.
Which of the two is better for you?
Repair gender, construct and case errors systematically.
Choose gender and case together before the explanation appears.
Use “which?” to navigate choices in schedules, shopping, travel and preferences.
أَيَّةَ مَادَّةٍ سَتَخْتَارُ؟ أَيُّ يَوْمٍ يُنَاسِبُكَ؟ فِي أَيَّةِ قَاعَةٍ سَتَكُونُ الْحِصَّةُ؟
Identify the gender and case evidence in each question.
Have a partner read eight questions. Sort them into masculine أَيّ and feminine أَيَّة, then identify whether each form is nominative, accusative or genitive.
Ask about a day, subject, city, sport, colour and book. Give a full answer and one reason each time.
Change broad questions with مَا / مَاذَا into precise “which?” questions for a known list.
Write a dialogue in which one person chooses a course, journey, item or activity from several options.
[callout] Success checklist: Include three masculine and three feminine أَيّ/أَيَّة questions, all three cases, two prepositions, one أَيُّهُمَا stretch form and complete reasoned answers.
Show that you can coordinate meaning, gender, construct and case.
- Use masculine أَيّ and feminine أَيَّة.
- Build the construct phrase with a genitive noun.
- Inflect the interrogative form for nominative, accusative and genitive roles.
- Distinguish “which?” from open مَا / مَاذَا questions.
- Ask and answer choice questions in practical contexts.
Spaced revisit: select six nouns from different Cambridge topics and build one nominative, accusative or prepositional “which?” question for each.
